# The subgroup generated by actual relative-root points

Author: Worker 1331.

This derived construction names the abstract subgroup already appearing in
`SimplyConnectedKneserTitsFactorStatement`. For an affine group scheme `G` over
an arbitrary field `k : Type u` and a torus homomorphism `i : S.toGrp ⟶ G`,
`relativeRootGeneratedSubgroup i` is `Subgroup.closure` of the union of the
base-point groups of `RelativeRoot.subgroup i α` for `α ∈ relativeRoots i`.
This is subgroup generation in `G(k)`.

The inclusion of every root group and the universal property follow directly
from subgroup closure. If the underlying torus map is a monomorphism, every
rational normalizer point normalizes this generated subgroup. The proof uses
`RelativeRoot.normalizer_conj_mem` to send a generator to the group for its
Weyl-translated character, and `weylAction_mapsTo_relativeRoots` to verify that
the new character is a relative root. The centralizer inclusion follows
because whole-torus centralizer points are normalizer points.

For a connected reductive group and an actual maximal split torus,
`dynamicUnipotent_le_relativeRootGeneratedSubgroup` applies the published
`RelativeRoot.dynamicUnipotent_le_of_disjoint_positive_rays`. It retains that
theorem's local hypothesis that distinct indivisible positive roots have
disjoint positive integral rays. The cocharacter is arbitrary in this
containment result.

`relativeRootGeneratedSubgroup_normal_of_bruhat` retains three local inputs:
the equality of the cocharacter centralizer with the whole-torus centralizer,
`HasRationalBruhatDecomposition i ν`, and containment of the dynamic
unipotent points in the generated subgroup. The published Bruhat point
reduction writes any rational point as `a * n * b * z`, with `a,b` in the
dynamic radical, `n` in the torus normalizer and `z` in the centralizer.
Each of these four factors normalizes the generated subgroup. Its normalizer
is therefore the whole group, proving normality.

The disjoint-positive-rays corollary supplies the centralizer equality using
the proved `genericCentralizer` and radical containment using the result
above. It assumes connected reductivity, maximality of the split torus,
genericity of the chosen cocharacter, actual rational Bruhat decomposition,
and disjoint positive rays. The opposite-factor-pairs corollary replaces the
ray hypothesis by `RelativeRoot.HasOppositeFactorPairs i`, using the
published integral-coroot argument in `RootRayFromFactorPairs`.

The provenance is internal: the module packages the target's existing
subgroup and composes the cited Library proofs. It proves neither rational
Bruhat decomposition nor opposite-factor-pair existence, and supplies no
unconditional normality or Kneser–Tits theorem. All such remaining premises
must be discharged before applying it in the unconditional target.
